Milejczyce Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Milejczyce, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are recorded in Milejczyce from the late 16th century, with the community developing significantly in the 18th; by 1921, 648 Jews (55%) were mostly murdered at Treblinka in late 1942. This cemetery was established in 1865 and remained in use until WWII; Poland formally closed it in 1964, with a 1981 government survey finding it 'very damaged, no visible traces.' A 2010 project, 'Instruction for the Return of the Matzevah,' by the 'Ę' Association for Creative Initiatives, encouraged residents to voluntarily return stolen tombstones; in 2020, further matzevot used during the war to build stables were recovered.
